statements.title: Injection and precursor supply
statements.summary: Rapid injection can concentrate precursor conversion near the start of a reaction, helping distinguish nucleation from subsequent growth. A short period of rapid precursor conversion can favour nucleation, while a later lower supply can favour growth on existing particles.

statements.title: Heating and precursor conversion
statements.summary: As a mixture is heated, precursor conversion and particle growth can change at different rates. Different activation barriers can make these rates change differently as temperature rises, allowing nucleation and growth to overlap.

statements.title: Successive precursor additions
statements.summary: Successive precursor additions provide a way to control the supply of species used for surface growth. Alternating access to the needed elements can favour addition to existing surfaces, while precursor reactivity and surface accessibility influence incorporation.

statements.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
statements.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.

statements.title: Formation from dissolved precursors
statements.summary: When dissolved species become supersaturated with respect to a solid, nucleation and growth can compete with continued precursor conversion. Mixing, complexation and solution chemistry can change that balance.

statements.title: Building a gel network
statements.summary: Sol-gel processing connects molecular or colloidal building blocks into an extended network. Network formation and solvent removal influence how the wet material evolves during further processing.

statements.title: Contact and transport in solids
statements.summary: Solid-state conversion depends on contact between reactants and transport across their interfaces. Mechanical activation can create fresh interfaces and defects, which can help subsequent chemical conversion.

statements.title: Arrival and motion at a growth surface
statements.summary: In molecular beam epitaxy, incident species reach a surface where adsorption, surface motion and incorporation compete. A species that remains on the surface long enough can migrate to a growth site, while desorption competes with incorporation.

statements.title: Precursor delivery and surface chemistry
statements.summary: Vapour-deposition methods separate precursor delivery from reactions at or near a surface. Adsorbed precursors can react, exchange ligands or desorb, with surface coverage and delivery affecting which processes dominate.

statements.title: Supply to a surface
statements.summary: During deposition, incoming species can be incorporated, move across a surface or leave it again. Source supply and the state of the receiving surface can therefore affect growth in different ways.

statements.title: Charge transfer at an interface
statements.summary: Electrochemical conversion couples interfacial charge transfer to chemical change. Transport of reactants and the state of the interface can influence where material forms.

statements.title: Microwave coupling and heating
statements.summary: Microwave fields couple to materials through their electrical response and can heat different parts of a reaction mixture differently. Polarization and mobile charges dissipate field energy, so heating depends on the liquid, dissolved species and other absorbing materials.

statements.title: Reduction and particle formation
statements.summary: Reduction can convert dissolved precursor species into material able to nucleate or grow. Precursor coordination and reductant reactivity can change the supply of those species.

statements.title: A reaction medium with chemical roles
statements.summary: A polyol medium can participate in precursor coordination as well as transporting heat and dissolved species. Whether it also acts as a reductant depends on the reactants and reaction conditions.

statements.title: Conversion of a precursor
statements.summary: Thermal decomposition changes a precursor into species available for further reaction or growth. Bond cleavage and ligand transformations can change the supply of growth species, with competing pathways set by the precursor and medium.

statements.title: Growth on existing particles
statements.summary: Existing seeds provide surfaces where incoming material can be incorporated. Growth on available seed surfaces competes with formation of new nuclei when the supply of reactive species is high enough.

statements.title: Changing cations in an existing solid
statements.summary: Cation exchange changes the cation population of an existing material while transport and interface motion govern the transformation. Retention of an anion framework or particle shape depends on the particular system.

statements.title: Condensation and return of solvent
statements.summary: Reflux returns condensed vapour to a heated liquid and can limit net solvent loss. Condensation balances evaporation by returning solvent, while dissolved species continue to react in the liquid.

statements.title: Reaction in dispersed liquid domains
statements.summary: Microemulsions organize reactants into small liquid domains separated by interfaces. Exchange between domains and interfacial chemistry can matter alongside the chemistry within each domain.

statements.title: Transport in a flowing reaction
statements.summary: Flow geometry changes how reactants mix and how long material remains in different parts of a device. Diffusion and interfacial transport can therefore matter even when the overall feed composition is unchanged.

statements.title: Carboxylic-acid and carboxylate ligands
statements.summary: Carboxylic acids and carboxylates can associate with metal-containing surfaces and solution species through their oxygen groups. The hydrocarbon part of a long-chain ligand can favour dispersion in a compatible solvent, while acid-base equilibria influence how its head group associates.

statements.title: Amine coordination
statements.summary: An amine nitrogen can donate electron density to suitable solution species or surface sites. Donation from the nitrogen lone pair and competition with other ligands can change precursor speciation and surface association.

statements.title: Phosphines and precursor solutions
statements.summary: Elemental selenium can react with organophosphines to form soluble phosphorus-selenium-containing precursor species. Organic substituents can make these species compatible with an organic medium, while their composition and reactivity depend on the phosphine and preparation conditions.

statements.title: Phosphine-oxide coordination
statements.summary: A phosphine oxide can interact with suitable precursor or surface sites through its oxygen donor. Competition among oxygen-donor ligands can change precursor coordination and the availability of surface sites.

statements.title: A medium for transport
statements.summary: A solvent described as non-coordinating primarily provides a medium for heat and mass transport rather than being selected as a strong coordinating ligand. Heat transfer, viscosity and the solubility of precursors and ligands can affect mixing and material transport.

statements.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
statements.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.

statements.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
statements.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.

statements.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
statements.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.

statements.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
statements.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.

statements.title: Ligands in solution and at surfaces
statements.summary: Ligands can associate with dissolved species and particle surfaces, affecting their interactions with the surrounding liquid. A ligand shell compatible with the solvent can provide a barrier to close particle approach, helping a dispersion resist aggregation.

statements.title: Solvent and transport
statements.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.

statements.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
statements.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
